item.text:
**2B.1 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Best-supported reading: Srettha’s 2024 record favored diplomacy, compromise, and de-escalation where peaceful options were available. I found repeated use of ASEAN, bilateral talks, humanitarian channels, and border-management diplomacy. I did not find credible 2024 evidence that force was treated as the preferred first option.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 18, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand joined ASEAN’s call for an immediate cessation of violence, utmost restraint, defusing tensions, and safe humanitarian access in Myanmar. This is strong direct evidence for choosing de-escalation over force. | `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Thailand stresses the importance of upscaling humanitarian assistance along the Thai-Myanmar border at the Human Rights Council](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 4, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand said it was deeply concerned about Myanmar and backed humanitarian assistance, dialogue, reconciliation, and a return to democracy. This is direct evidence of preferring peaceful alternatives where they existed. | `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Special Envoy of ASEAN Chair on Myanmar welcomes successful pilot project of humanitarian initiative between Thailand and Myanmar during his meeting with Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs of Thailand](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 26, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand advanced a cross-border humanitarian pilot with Myanmar Red Cross participation and AHA Centre technical support. That shows a practical compromise track rather than coercive first-response behavior. | `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Vice Foreign Minister Sihasak meets with Special Envoy of ASEAN Chair on Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/pr210424-2) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 24, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/pr210424-2 | Thailand and the ASEAN Chair’s Special Envoy agreed ASEAN needed to step up engagement to maintain centrality, and stressed de-escalation and cessation of hostilities in Myawaddy. This is explicit preference for diplomacy and channel-preservation. | `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Deputy Foreign Minister and National Security delegation visit Mae Sot to receive the latest update on the Thailand-Myanmar border situation](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 23, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand sent a high-level team including foreign affairs, defense, armed forces, and NSC officials to receive updates and support local agencies at the border, rather than defaulting to force. The record shows crisis management through coordination. | `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Thailand pushed for seamless connectivity, green agenda, regional peace and stability at the ASEAN-Australia Special Summit](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/thailand-pushed-for-seamless-connectivity-green-ag?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 6, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/thailand-pushed-for-seamless-connectivity-green-ag?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand highlighted regional peace and stability, alongside cooperation on connectivity, green policy, and humanitarian assistance in Myanmar. This is broader support for diplomacy over force-first instincts. | `2B.1` |
| [Prime Minister holds bilateral talks with Bangladeshi Prime Minister during her trip to Thailand](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/pm-meets-with-pm-of-bangladesh-2024-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 26, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/pm-meets-with-pm-of-bangladesh-2024-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand and Bangladesh pursued FTA talks, port connectivity, tourism, customs cooperation, and humanitarian discussion on Myanmar/Rohingya issues. This is consistent with compromise and nonviolent statecraft where peaceful alternatives existed. | `2B.1` |

**Search gap**

- I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Srettha preferred force as the first option in a crisis where diplomacy was available.
- The strongest relevant evidence comes from Myanmar-border diplomacy, humanitarian access, ASEAN engagement, and bilateral bargaining.
- I did not find a clear contrary case, so the record supports a de-escalatory reading rather than a mixed or force-first one.
